messages.author: 4d3491ebd845aea4
messages.subject: Statistical Analysis Question
parts:
Hi Everyone,
I am trying to do some statistical analysis on my data that contains
time course of treatments (6 time points) for three biological
replicates. In each biological replicate I have multiple proteins
identified and their corresponding abundance at each time point. I
would like to determine which proteins have significant abundance
changes throughout the time points. I have considered an ANOVA test
and KPPS time series significance test, but I'm not sure either is the
correct test that I should be doing. Are there any R packages that
are available and suitable for this type of analysis? Please advise.

Thanks,
M. Violet Lee

> identified and their corresponding abundance at each time point.  I
> would like to determine which proteins have significant abundance
> changes throughout the time points.  I have considered an ANOVA test
> and KPPS time series significance test, but I'm not sure either is the

This type of repeated measures over time is called longitudinal data
and there are specific techniques for it. If you have a largish
number of proteins you may consider using a mixed-effects model with
random effects for the slopes and intercepts for this. See, for
example
http://lme4.r-forge.r-project.org/slides/2009-07-21-Seewiesen/5LongitudinalD.pdf
